claim: The sample demo never reads or changes the user's real library state.
sandbox: fresh browser context with a sentinel real-library key; use search and reset; assert only demo:rsl:library-state:v1 changes

claim: Catalogue data is stored on the user's computer and catalogue work makes no passive network request.
where: landing privacy section, desktop footer, privacy page, README
sandbox: fresh installed-app web preview; add an EPUB; assert it is written to rsl:library-state:v1 and all observed requests stay on the app origin

claim: The app makes no passive network requests. The website and demo use no analytics, advertising, third-party scripts, or cookies; the landing page contacts only GitHub's public releases API for current download links.
where: landing facts and privacy section, privacy page, README
sandbox: serve the local build through the production origin; mock the GitHub releases API; record landing, demo, and idle-app requests; assert GitHub is the only third-party request and the cookie jar is empty

claim: Catalogue, collection, USB, WebDAV, and Markdown tools require no purchase or product account.
where: landing facts and privacy section, desktop WebDAV panel, terms, README
sandbox: fresh demo without a license; assert catalogue, collections, notes, and WebDAV controls are enabled and no checkout link exists

claim: Catalogue, collection, and Markdown tools reopen offline after the first demo visit.
sandbox: fresh browser context; load /demo/ online under its service worker; set context offline; reload and assert sample catalogue state

claim: The recursive scan reads EPUB title, author, series, and cover status, includes PDFs, ignores other files, and excludes protected PDFs.
where: landing workflow and preview, desktop catalogue, README
sandbox: temporary nested library with a metadata-rich EPUB, a protected PDF, and an unrelated text file; scan through the native core and assert all observed fields and eligibility

claim: Scanning book metadata does not rewrite the source file.
sandbox: temporary source PDF; record bytes, scan it through the native inspection path, and assert exact bytes remain

claim: PDF titles and authors stored as UTF-16 or PDFDocEncoding are decoded without replacement characters.
sandbox: temporary generated PDF with Unicode title and author; scan the file and assert exact decoded values

claim: Collection order becomes numbered, device-safe folders and filenames.
sandbox: clean sample demo; inspect its ordered collection and assert all three Unicode-safe planned filenames in order

claim: USB sync preserves source bytes, verifies copied bytes, and skips an unchanged repeat copy.
where: desktop transfer panel, privacy page, README
sandbox: temporary source and device directories; copy twice; compare source and destination bytes and inspect the device manifest

claim: An incomplete USB staging copy never replaces an existing verified destination file.
sandbox: temporary source and device directories with an existing good destination; inject a partial staging write; assert the good file remains and the staging file is removed

claim: WebDAV setup needs no product license, does not persist its address, username, or password, clears the password after every attempt, and shows recovery guidance.
where: landing privacy section, desktop WebDAV panel, privacy page, README
sandbox: fresh installed-app web preview with mocked native IPC; exercise failed and successful checks plus upload; inspect UI, IPC payloads, password field, and all local storage

claim: WebDAV enforces HTTPS except for local testing, checks the destination, creates collection folders, authenticates, and uploads exact selected bytes.
where: desktop WebDAV panel, privacy page, README
sandbox: temporary source plus a local HTTP WebDAV fixture; assert PROPFIND, MKCOL, authenticated PUT path/body, remote error guidance, and rejection of a deceptive non-local HTTP host

claim: Imports Markdown, JSON, KOReader sidecar, and embedded PDF annotations.
sandbox: temporary Markdown, JSON, KOReader Lua, and generated annotated PDF fixtures; import each through the native path and assert quote/note content

claim: Exports imported highlights as plain Markdown.
where: landing workflow and preview, desktop notes panel, README
sandbox: open /demo/ from clean storage; export bundled highlights; inspect the downloaded Markdown contents

claim: A release manifest names installers for macOS Intel and Apple silicon, Windows, and Linux, with a SHA-256 checksum for each.
sandbox: temporary fake platform bundles; run the production manifest generator; assert all required platform URLs and exact SHA-256 entries
